items.title: 68427_Harry Edison oral history interview
items.q: So I think my first was Jimmy Forrest, Joe Benjamin and Jimmy Jones was on piano

ctx.x: Oh, yes, you almost wanted to --

Yeah, wanted to go to New York, anyway. So I think my first was Jimmy Forrest, Joe Benjamin and Jimmy Jones was on piano, and oh, what's the drummer's name in New York, not Elvin because Elvin came latter. He played with Billy Eckstine for a long time. Good drummer.* Anyway, they opened up with me. And it was a fantastic night, you know.
And Joe Benjamin, after he left, then I got Tommy Potter and Tommy Flanagan and Elvin Jones.

items.title: 69537_Jimmy Jones oral history interview
items.q: We had Ben Webster, Harry Edison on the date

ctx.x: But it's different with the -- oh, the first time I did some conducting for strings was with Joe
Williams. We had Ben Webster, Harry Edison on the date, you know, just to put the jazz sound in it, you know.

items.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

ctx.x: Yeah, in fact at Birdland I had Tommy Flanagan playing with me. And he calls me and he says, “I got a substitute coming in for tonight, his name is Roland Hanna.” I said, “Man I never heard of him.” He said, “Well, he’s a good player.” So I said, “Has he been around New York long?” He said, “No, I think he just came in from Washington or something.” When I went to club he was already there. He says, “Man, I’d like to get a draw.” I said, “Well I haven’t even heard you play, I don’t even know whether I’m going to…
was such a great piano player and Elvin Jones--he left my band and went to Coltrane. And everybody after the band broke up went someplace else. Flanagan, I had Jimmy Jones
Roland played with you for…it wasn’t just that one period. He stayed with you for a while.
